tldr: Azure Service Bus Premium can now combine partitioned throughput with cross-region geo-replication, improving resilience for high-throughput messaging.
Azure Fluid Relay retires on February 2, 2027; identify dependent workloads and plan a migration.
AI agent tasks can consume 10–50 times the tokens of a basic chat prompt, so per-task costs deserve explicit limits and monitoring.

top.title: Service Bus geo-replication reaches GA for partitioned namespaces
top.summary: Azure Service Bus Premium now supports geo-replication on partitioned namespaces, replicating messages and metadata to a secondary region while retaining partitioning's throughput benefits.
top.why: Revisit your messaging resilience design: you can now pair higher-throughput partitioned namespaces with regional replication.

top.title: Azure Fluid Relay retires on February 2, 2027
top.summary: Azure Fluid Relay will reach end of availability on February 2, 2027; the Fluid Framework will remain available as open source.
top.why: Inventory Fluid Relay dependencies now and plan a replacement or self-hosting approach before the service shuts down.

top.title: PostgreSQL Flexible Server can switch to private endpoint networking
top.summary: Existing Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server instances using VNet integration can now move to a private endpoint-capable network configuration.
top.why: If delegated-subnet networking constrains your design, assess this migration path before building new connectivity around the existing setup.

top.title: AKS flex nodes preview lets clusters use external and edge compute
top.summary: AKS flex nodes can connect user-managed VMs or on-premises servers—including compute in other regions or at the edge—to an existing cluster without adding another Kubernetes control plane; portal support is now in preview.
top.why: For hybrid or edge workloads, evaluate whether one cluster can simplify operations, but treat the preview as an early design option rather than a production default.

also.title: Azure Migrate previews NAS discovery for Dell PowerScale and NetApp ONTAP
also.summary: Azure Migrate can discover and assess Dell PowerScale and NetApp ONTAP network-attached storage to help plan migrations to Azure.

also.title: Azure Site Recovery for Azure Local is generally available
also.summary: Azure Site Recovery can now protect supported Windows and Linux VMs running on Azure Local by replicating them for disaster recovery.

also.title: Azure Storage Actions adds task updates, controls, and case-sensitive matching
also.summary: Storage Actions now propagates task-definition changes automatically, offers more execution controls, and supports case-sensitive matching.

also.title: Databricks serverless jobs preview supports environment variables
also.summary: An Azure Community post describes the Lakeflow Jobs beta feature for using environment variables in serverless jobs instead of manually switching notebook settings or embedding tokens in code.

also.title: Microsoft plans to retire Defender for IoT OT security in October 2029
also.summary: Microsoft has announced a three-year transition period before deprecating the operational technology security component of Defender for IoT in October 2029.

top.title: AI agent coding tasks may use 10–50 times more tokens than chat
top.summary: A coding agent can plan, generate code, run tests, and retry; one task may consume 10 to 50 times the tokens of a basic chat prompt.
top.why: Model agent workloads as task-level costs, not just chat-sized requests, and set budgets and monitoring around completed work.

top.title: OpenAI program will offer up to 1,000 MW of data-center power relief
top.summary: OpenAI says its Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to support grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs; its first planned pilot in Georgia could free up to 1,000 megawatts during emergencies.
top.why: When assessing AI capacity plans, account for grid constraints and demand-response commitments alongside available power and compute.

top.title: Uber built an MCP gateway to govern access to 5,000-plus agent tools
top.summary: Uber's MCP Gateway standardizes agent access across more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools, with access controls, sensitive-data redaction, response filtering, and separate registration and execution paths.
top.why: If agent tool access is spreading across teams, evaluate a governed gateway pattern before each agent connects to services independently.

also.title: Devin adds hierarchical budgets that can stop an agent mid-task
also.summary: Cognition has added hierarchical spending limits to Devin, allowing teams to budget agent work and cut it off when a limit is reached.
